rv.q: Working with great economy, Walker’s “Covenant” is an auspicious New York debut for a playwright who clearly has a gift for richly textured work.

Either approach is fine, but trying to do both at once requires a technical balancing act, a puppet-master’s exacting control over our sense of what’s real—when to pull the audience one way, and when to pull us back the other way—that Walker hasn’t quite nailed.
With “Covenant,” Mr. York has given us briskly entertaining food for thought about the demons that haunt us all, individually and collectively.
Covenant finds redemption in its reworking of the possession narrative.
Covenant is absolutely an enjoyable piece to watch.

Under Tiffany Nichole Greene’s direction, Covenant is genuinely scary, and that it achieves this for an audience inundated with high-budget, digital effects–driven entertainment is a testament to the theatrical craft on display.

cn.t: York Walker's Southern gothic thriller earns praise for its potent atmosphere and electric performances, with critics highlighting the production's inventive staging, swift direction, and ability to deliver genuine scares in an intimate setting.
